items.stem: Which of the following is WRONG about variation of contracts under Ethiopian law of contract? ______
items.answer:
A. Judges are obliged to vary a contract made between parties having a special relationship when there is change of circumstance.

Under Article 1766 of the Civil Code, the court *may* vary a contract where a special relationship exists and the parties do not agree, compelling them to deal with each other in accordance with equity. This is a discretionary power, not an obligation. Under Article 1763 of the Civil Code, the court may not vary a contract or alter its terms on the ground of equity except in such cases as are expressly provided by law.

items.stem: Among the following one is NOT NECESSARY to look into when the courts interpret the contract of parties. Which one is it? _____
items.answer:
B. Ethnicity and religion of parties.

Under Article 1734 of the Civil Code, where contract provisions are ambiguous, the common intention of the parties shall be sought, and their general conduct before and after the contract may be considered. Article 1732 of the Civil Code states that contracts shall be interpreted in accordance with good faith, having regard to the loyalty and confidence that should exist between the parties according to business practice. Article 1736 of the Civil Code mandates that contract provisions be interpreted through one another, with each provision given the meaning required by the whole contract, and ambiguous terms given the more likely meaning considering the subject matter. Furthermore, Article 1737 of the Civil Code provides for positive interpretation, meaning provisions capable of two meanings should be given a meaning that renders them effective rather than ineffective. The ethnicity and religion of the parties are not mentioned as factors to consider in contract interpretation.

items.stem: All statements are true except the one about protection of creditors under the Ethiopian contract law.
items.answer:
C. The creditor always has the burden of proving that the apparent act is a simulation to challenge debtor’s transaction.

Under Article 1994 of the Civil Code, a creditor may have established, by judicial decision, that a transaction effected by a debtor was a simulated one which, by agreement, was not intended to be carried out. This implies that the creditor needs to prove the simulation. However, the statement says the creditor *always* has the burden, which may not be true in all circumstances, especially if there are legal presumptions or other mechanisms that shift the burden of proof.

Under Article 1987 of the Civil Code, the performance by the debtor of his obligations shall be secured by all his assets, with the exception of those which cannot be attached at law. This means that not all assets of the debtor may be subject to attachment.

Under Article 1993 of the Civil Code, a creditor may, with the authorisation of the court, exercise as representative of the debtor all the rights of the debtor so as to prevent such impoverishment of the debtor as would jeopardize the payment of the debt. This provision, along with others like Article 1995 (Debtor's fraud) and Article 1996 (Fraudulent acts), indicates that legal provisions generally favor the creditor in protecting their rights against a debtor's actions that could jeopardize the debt.

items.answer:
B. Partial performance of the indivisible obligation by one of the debtor validly discharges his part of obligation.

Under Article 1917 of the Civil Code, the provisions regarding joint obligations apply by analogy to obligations that are indivisible due to their nature. However, Article 1918 of the Civil Code states that obligations which are neither joint nor indivisible are divided between the persons liable, and each debtor is liable for their lawful share. This implies that for an indivisible obligation, partial performance by one debtor would not discharge their part, as the obligation itself cannot be divided.

items.stem: One is necessarily a characteristic of companies generally EXCEPT.
items.answer:
E. Less centralized management structure.

Justification:
Companies generally have a centralized management structure, as evidenced by the responsibilities and powers of the board of directors in a share company (Article 315 of the Commercial Code) and the manager in a private limited company (Article 532 of the Commercial Code). The other options are generally characteristics of companies. Limited liability is a characteristic of private limited companies (Article 495 of the Commercial Code) and share companies (Article 245 of the Commercial Code). Continued existence is a characteristic of partnerships (Article 222 of the Commercial Code), and by extension, companies. Distinct legal personality is also a characteristic of partnerships (Article 222 of the Commercial Code), and thus companies. Transferability of shares is a characteristic of share companies, though private limited companies may not issue transferable securities (Article 295 of the Commercial Code).

items.stem: Among the following one is a common characteristics of joint venture under the
items.answer: C. Under Article 172(2) of the Commercial Code (Proclamation No. 1243/2021), a joint venture is formed by an agreement concluded among members that is not disclosed to third parties. This implies that it need not be known by third parties. The same article also states that a joint venture is formed by an agreement, which suggests that an agreement between partners may be made in writing, as supported by Article 1726 of the Civil Code (Proclamation No. 165/1960) which allows for agreements to be in writing even when not legally required. items.stem: Among the following, one is not necessarily a general mechanism of protecting
items.answer:
D. Encouraging firms to merge so as to strengthen their economic muscle for contributing to the economic development.

Justification: The provided legal texts discuss consumer protection in terms of preventing unfair trade practices (አንቀጽ 719 of the Revised Criminal Code, Art. 2057 of the Civil Code), ensuring information disclosure in electronic transactions (Article 28 of the Electronic Transaction Proclamation), and setting quality standards (አንቀጽ 395 of the Revised Criminal Code). There is no mention of encouraging firm mergers as a mechanism for consumer protection. In fact, some provisions address anti-competitive practices, which mergers could potentially exacerbate if not properly regulated.

items.stem: Suppose that A, B, C and D have established a firm called A, B & their friends’ General
items.answer:
D. Mr. A can transfer full rights of his share to Mr. X without the assent of his fellow partners.

Under Article 219(1) of the Commercial Code, shares may not be transferred to third parties except with the consent of all general partners and a majority of the limited partners. While Article 197(1) of the Commercial Code allows a partner to transfer beneficial interests and rights in his share to a third party without the consent of other partners, Article 197(2) clarifies that such a transfer does not bind the partnership and the third party does not acquire full rights of a partner. Therefore, transferring full rights of a share requires the consent of the other partners.

items.stem: Under the Ethiopian property law regime, the right of preemption is;
items.answer: C. A right of pre-emption may not be created for more than ten years, since such agreement affects the public interest for the free transfer of goods. Under Article 1419 of the Civil Code, a right of pre-emption shall be exercised within two months from the beneficiary being informed of the owner's intention to sell. The parties may extend this period to one year by agreement, but if a period exceeding one year has been agreed, it shall be reduced to one year.

items.answer: C. Possession is understood in Ethiopia in terms of only a physical control a person may have on a thing. Under Article 1140 of the Civil Code, possession consists in the actual control which a person exercises over a thing. This definition does not limit possession to only physical control, implying that other forms of control may also constitute possession.

items.stem: Which of the following is not the right of a joint owner of a thing?
items.answer:
D. A Joint owner can block any collective decision regarding a jointly owned thing.

items.stem: According to the federal revised family code, which of the following is false about ascertainment of paternity?
items.answer:
A. The legal rules concerning maternity can any time be derogated by agreement.

Under Article 123 of the amharic-family-code, the provisions of this law regarding the ascertainment of paternity and maternity cannot be altered by agreement, unless the law explicitly permits it. Therefore, the statement that legal rules concerning maternity can be derogated by agreement is false.

items.stem: Which one of the following statement best describe things makeup of succession.
items.answer:
E. All

Under Article 826 of the Civil Code, the succession of a deceased person includes the rights and obligations that form the inheritance, unless such rights and obligations terminate with the death of the deceased. Article 1005 of the Civil Code furtherE. All

Under Article 826 of the Civil Code, the succession of a deceased person includes the rights and obligations that form the inheritance, unless such rights and obligations terminate with the death of the deceased. Article 1005 of the Civil Code further clarifies that the liquidator establishes what the succession is made up of by drawing up an inventory. This inventory includes both assets and liabilities, as indicated by Article 1006 of the Civil Code. Therefore, the succession encompasses all rights and duties left behind by the deceased, as well as hereditary estates. Monies due in performance of a contract of life insurance to which the deceased determined a beneficiary and pensions payable to the deceased after retirement age would also be considered part of the deceased's estate or rights that pass to heirs, depending on the specific terms and applicable laws.

Regarding the validity forms of a public will, Article 881 of the Civil Code states that a public will must be written by the testator or by any person under the testator's dictation. It is only effective if it is read in the presence of the testator and four witnesses, and mention of this formality and its date is made in the will. The testator and the witnesses must immediately sign the will or affix their thumb mark thereon.

items.answer:
B. It becomes effective after the death of the person.

Under Article 826 of the Civil Code, when a person dies, their succession opens at the place of their principal residence at the time of death. items.stem: Which of the following is different among the given alternatives?
items.answer:
B. Vicarious liability.

Product liability, strict liability, and the absence of fault not being a defense are all related concepts under Ethiopian law concerning liability for manufactured goods. Under Article 2085 of the Civil Code, a person who manufactures and sells goods for profit is liable for damage caused by their normal use. Article 2086 further clarifies that those legally liable for damage caused by manufactured goods cannot escape liability by proving they committed no offense, or that the cause of damage was unknown, or that it was not in their power to prevent the damage, or that the damage was due to a third party. This indicates a form of strict liability where the absence of fault is not a defense. Liability is imposed on producers in these cases.

Vicarious liability, on the other hand, refers to a situation where one person is held responsible for the actions or omissions of another person. While the Commercial Code, Article 228, mentions that a company can be held jointly and severally liable with a partner or employee for damages caused during the performance of the company's work, this is a distinct concept from the liability of a producer for defects in manufactured goods.

items.stem: Which one is not true about extra contractual liability law?
items.answer:
A. In tort law all types of harm attract legal liability.

Under Article 2028 of the Civil Code, "Whosoever causes damage to another by an offence shall make it good." This general principle indicates that causing damage through an offense leads to liability. However, the statement "all types of harm attract legal liability" is too broad and not explicitly supported as universally true for every conceivable harm without qualification.

B. Existence of damage is a precondition in order to claim remedy in tort law.

Under Article 2028 of the Civil Code, liability arises when a person "causes damage to another by an offence." This implies that damage is a prerequisite for liability in extra-contractual matters. Additionally, Article 1892 of the Civil Code, while discussing penalties, distinguishes between actual damage and the penalty due, further suggesting that damage is a core concept in claiming remedies.

C. Age is a defense that exempt from liability.

Article 303 of the Family Code states that "Where the minor had caused damage to another person by his unlawful acts or enriched himself unlawfully, he shall be liable in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Code relating to Extra-Contractual Liability and Unlawful Enrichment." This indicates that a minor can be held liable for damage caused by unlawful acts, suggesting that age alone does not automatically exempt from extra-contractual liability.

Therefore, the statement that is not true is A.

items.stem: Which of the following statements is correct among the given alternatives?
items.answer:
A. Fault of the victim totally exempts the tort-feasor or at least reduces the extent of liability that the latter owes to the victim.

Under Article 2086 of the Civil Code, persons legally liable for creating an abnormal risk or for damage caused by animals, buildings, machines, motor vehicles, or manufactured goods may be relieved of their liability entirely or in part if the damage is due solely or partly to the fault of the victim. Furthermore, under Article 2098 of the Civil Code, where damage is partly due to the fault of the victim, the victim is entitled to partial compensation only. The extent to which the damage shall be made good is determined by considering all circumstances, particularly the contribution and gravity of the faults committed.

items.stem: All are correct about the basic principles of criminal law except?
items.answer:
D. The principle of equality implies equality of treatment although they are not in equal circumstances.

Under Article 4 of the Amharic Revised Criminal Code, criminal law applies equally to all without distinction based on social status, race, ethnicity, color, gender, language, religion, political or other opinion, wealth, origin, or other status. Differences among offenders are made only when there is a fundamental right stipulated in this law, originating from international law or the constitution, or when this law stipulates that the severity of the crime, the degree of fault, or the age, circumstances, or special personal characteristics of the offender, or the danger the crime has caused to society, should be taken into account. This indicates that while the law applies equally, treatment can differ based on specific circumstances. Therefore, the statement that equality implies equality of treatment *although they are not in equal circumstances* is incorrect, as differences in circumstances can lead to differentiated treatment under the law.

Under Article 2 of the English Revised Criminal Code, the principle of legality states that the Court may not treat as a crime and punish any act or omission which is not prohibited by law, nor impose penalties or measures other than those prescribed by law. This supports the statement that according to the principle of legality, there is no crime and punishment unless specified by law.

items.stem: Which one of the following is not the principal jurisdiction of the Ethiopian criminal law?
items.answer:
A. Crimes committed by members of the Ethiopian defense forces against the ‘ordinary law’ of a foreign country.

Under Article 15 of the Revised Criminal Code, where a member of the Ethiopian Defence Forces commits a crime against the ordinary law in a foreign country, they are subject to the ordinary law and territorial jurisdiction of that country if arrested and tried there. If they take refuge in Ethiopia, they are tried in accordance with the provisions of the Code. This indicates that the primary jurisdiction for such crimes is the foreign country where the crime was committed, not Ethiopia's principal jurisdiction.

items.stem: Which one of the following choices is wrong about material element (actus-reus) of a crime?
items.answer:
C. The existence of bad thought to violate criminal law by itself is sufficient to punish a person although not manifested.

Under Article 23 of the Revised Criminal Code, a crime is only completed when all its legal, material, and moral ingredients are present. This indicates that a "bad thought" alone, without a manifested act, is not sufficient for a crime to be complete. Furthermore, Article 23 states that a crime is an act which is prohibited and made punishable by law, and an act consists of the commission of what is prohibited or the omission of what is prescribed by law. This emphasizes the requirement of an external manifestation or conduct.

Under Article 230 of the Revised Criminal Code, amnesty prevents the initiation or continuation of any criminal prosecution from the time it is granted. If a penalty has been imposed, amnesty cancels the penalty and any other criminal consequences, and the conviction is erased from the criminal record. This indicates that amnesty can be granted before or after conviction. In contrast, Article 229 of the Revised Criminal Code states that pardon applies to a penalty imposed by a court, implying it is a post-conviction procedure.

items.stem: One of the following categories of individuals is absolutely free from the provisions of the criminal law of Ethiopia. Who are they?
items.answer:
C. Persons under the age of nine

Under Article 48 of the Revised Criminal Code, criminal responsibility is attributed to the offender who is accountable for their actions. However, this article also mentions exceptions for individuals due to age, illness, developmental delay, or severe mental impairment. While the article does not explicitly state that persons under nine are absolutely free from criminal law, it implies that age is a factor in criminal responsibility.

Article 53 of the Revised Criminal Code states that special provisions apply to young offenders aged nine to fifteen years. This implies that those below nine years old are treated differently and are not subject to the same criminal provisions as older individuals. Article 144 of the 2004 Criminal Code further clarifies that for young persons aged nine to fifteen, the court will order one of the precautionary measures outlined in the law. This reinforces the idea that individuals under nine are not held criminally responsible in the same way.

citations.title: Crimes Against Humanity
citations.content:
Crimes Against Humanity
Criminal liability of persons who commit crimes against humanity, so defined by international agreements ratified by Ethiopia and by other laws of Ethiopia, such as genocide, summary executions, forcible disappearances or torture shall not be barred by statute of limitation.

items.stem: One of the following is not the purpose of modern taxation. Which one?
items.answer:
B. To maximize income and wealth inequalities

The provided legal knowledge base does not contain a specific provision that directly outlines the purposes of modern taxation. However, based on the general principles reflected in the economic objectives of the FDRE Constitution, maximizing income and wealth inequalities would contradict the stated goals of promoting equitable distribution of wealth. Under Article 10 of the FDRE Constitution, the government has a duty to ensure that all Ethiopians get equal opportunity to improve their economic condition and to promote equitable distribution of wealth among them.

C) Transfer pricing.

A tax evasion that occurs when two or more related organizations in different domiciles try to plan to avoid their tax liability is termed as Transfer Pricing. Under Article 2 of the Federal Income Tax Proclamation No. 979/2008, "Transfer Pricing" refers to transactions that are not arm's length transactions, where the Authority may distribute, apportion, or allocate income, gains, deductions, losses, or tax credits between the parties to reflect what would have been realized in an arm's length transaction. This article specifically addresses situations where one party is located in Ethiopia and another outside Ethiopia, and also allows for directives to apply to transactions wholly within Ethiopia.

items.stem: Which of the following may not fully considered as a binding source of international law?
items.answer:
D. Teachings/publications of concerned & known scholars

Under Article 7 of the Ethiopian Constitution, international agreements ratified by Ethiopia are part of the law of the land. Similarly, Article 4(1)(a) of the Federal Courts Proclamation No. 1234/2021 states that Federal Courts shall settle cases based on the Constitution, Federal Laws, and International Treaties to which Ethiopia is a party. These provisions indicate that international treaties and conventions are binding sources of law in Ethiopia. While the decisions of the ICJ and international customary laws are generally recognized as sources of international law, the teachings and publications of scholars are typically considered subsidiary means for determining rules of law, rather than binding sources themselves.

items.answer:
D) All of the above.

Under Article 18 of the Revised Criminal Code, Ethiopian law applies to crimes committed outside Ethiopia against an Ethiopian national (nationality principle) and to other crimes committed outside Ethiopia by a foreign national if the crime is punishable under Ethiopian law with death or rigorous imprisonment for not less than ten years (universality principle, in cases where extradition fails). The territoriality principle is a fundamental basis for jurisdiction, as indicated by the general application of the Code to crimes within Ethiopia and the specific provisions for extraterritorial jurisdiction.

items.stem: One of the following is not the power of the Prime Minister under the FDRE Constitution. Which one?
items.answer:
E.
Under Article 74 of the FDRE Constitution, the Prime Minister is the Chief Executive, the Chairman of the Council of Ministers, and the Commander-in-Chief of the national armed forces. He is also empowered to nominate Ministers to be appointed by the House of Peoples' Representatives. However, the power to proclaim laws in the Negarit Gazeta is vested in the President, upon recommendation by the Prime Minister, as stated in Article 71 of the FDRE Constitution.

items.stem: Which one of the following is not the nature of human rights?
items.answer:
C. They are endowment to all persons by the will of government.

Human rights and freedoms, emanating from the nature of mankind, are inviolable and inalienable. Under Article 7 of the FDRE Constitution of 1995, human rights are not granted by the will of the government but rather stem from the nature of mankind.

items.stem: Which one of the following is not the vulnerable segments of the society
items.answer:
D. None

Under Article 41 of the Ethiopian Constitution, the State has an obligation to provide rehabilitation and assistance to the physically and mentally disabled, the aged, and children who are left without parents or guardians. Additionally, Article 35 of the Constitution outlines specific rights for women, including affirmative measures to remedy historical inequality and discrimination. While refugees are not explicitly mentioned in these articles as a vulnerable segment requiring state assistance, the listed categories (children, the aged, and the disabled) are clearly identified as such. Therefore, none of the options provided (Women, Children, Refugees) are *not* vulnerable segments, as women and children are recognized as vulnerable in the Constitution.

items.stem: Which one of the following alternative best describe the natures, purpose and scope of law of civil procedure
items.answer:
A. A&B

Under Article 3345 of the Civil Code, the procedure to be followed by an arbitration tribunal is as prescribed by the Code of Civil Procedure. This indicates that the Civil Procedure Code serves as a means to enforce substantive laws. Additionally, Article 108 of the Family Code states that the provisions of the Civil Procedure Code of Ethiopia are applicable to disputes arising from matters provided in the Family Code, further supporting its role in the enforceability of rights and duties. While the provided articles do not explicitly state that the law is designed to secure the "just, speedy and inexpensive disposition of civil cases," the general purpose of procedural law is to facilitate the efficient administration of justice. The statement that it is "concerned with matters largely falling outside the environs of the courtrooms" is incorrect, as civil procedure primarily governs proceedings within the courts.

items.stem: Which one of the following alternative is true about qualifications of party to civil suit?
items.answer:
D. A&B

Under Article 33(1) of the Civil Procedure Code, any person capable under the law may be a party to a suit. Article 33(2) states that no person may be a plaintiff unless they have a vested interest in the subject-matter of the suit. Furthermore, Article 33(3) specifies that no person may be a defendant unless the plaintiff alleges some claim against them.

(3) No person may be a defendant unless the plaintiff alleges some claim against him.

citations.content:
የፌደራልና የክልል የመጀመሪያ ደረጃ ፍርድ ቤት የሥራ ክርክር ችሎት የሚከተሉትንና ሌሎች ተመሳሳይ የግል የሥራ ክርክር ጉዳዮችን ተቀብሎ የማየትና የመወሰን ሥልጣን ይኖረዋል:-

ለ) የሥራ ውል መቋረጥ የሚመለከቱ ክሶች፤
ሐ) የሥራ ሰዓትን፣ የተከፋይ ሂሣብን፣ ፈቃድንና ዕረፍትን የሚመለከቱ ክሶች፤ 
መ) የአገልግሎትና የስንብት ማስረጃ ሠርተፊኬት መስጠትን የሚመለከቱ ክሶች፣

citations.title: ጠቅላላ
citations.content:
ከሥራ ውል የሚመነጩ መብቶችና ግዴታዎች በዚህ ዘርፍ በተመለከተው አኳኋን ለጊዜው ሊታገዱ ይችላሉ፡፡ 
ከሥራ ውል የሚመነጩ መብቶችና ግዴታዎች ለጊዜው መታገድ የሥራ ውልን የሚያስቀር ወይም የሚያቋርጥ አይሆንም፤ ሆኖም:- 
ሀ) ሠራተኛው የመሥራት ግዴታ የለበትም፤ 
ለ) በዚህ አዋጅ ወይም በኅብረት ስምምነት በሌላ አኳኋን ካልተወሰነ በስተቀር አሠሪው ደመወዝ፣ ሌሎች ጥቅማ ጥቅሞች እና አበል የመክፈል ግዴታ አይኖርበትም፡፡

citations.title: የይርጋ ጊዜ መቋረጥ
citations.content:
የይርጋ ጊዜ በሚከተሉት ሁኔታዎች ይቋረጣል:- 
የሥራ ክርክርን ለሚወስን ባለሥልጣን ክስ ቀርቦ የመጨረሻ ውሣኔ እስከሚሰጥበት ቀን ድረስ፤ 
የአሠሪና ሠራተኛ ጉዳይ አዋጅን በሥራ ላይ ለማዋልና ለማስፈጸም ኃላፊነት ለተሰጠው ባለሥልጣን አቤቱታ ቀርቦ የመጨረሻ ውሣኔ በጽሑፍ እስከሚሰጥበት ቀን ድረስ፤ 
በይርጋ ጊዜ ተጠያቂ የሆነው ወገን የሌላውን መብት በጽሑፍ ሲያውቅለት ወይም በከፊል ሲፈጽምለት፤ ሆኖም በዚህ ምክንያት የይርጋ ጊዜው የተቋረጠ የመብት ጥያቄ በአጠቃላይ ከ፫ ጊዜ

He who alleges that an obligation is void, has been varied or is extinguished shall prove the facts causing such nullity, variation or extinction.

citations.content:
የሚከተሉት የሥራ ውልን ያለ ማስጠንቀቂያ ለማቋረጥ በቂ ምክንያቶች ይሆናሉ:- 
ሀ) አሠሪው ወይም የሥራ መሪው የሠራተኛውን ሰብአዊ ክብርና ሞራል የሚነካ ወይም በወንጀል ሕጉ መሠረት የሚያስቀጣ ሌላ አድራጎት የፈጸመበት እንደሆነ፤ 
ለ) ሠራተኛው በአሠሪው ወይም በሥራ መሪው ወሲባዊ ትንኮሳ ወይም ጥቃት የተፈጸመበት እንደሆነ፤ 
ሐ) ለሠራተኛው ደኅንነት ወይም ጤንነት የሚያሰጋና ሊደርስ የተቃረበ አደጋ መኖሩን አሠሪው እያወቀ ወይም አደጋውን ለመከላከል የሚያስፈልጉ እርምጃዎች

items.stem: Identify the wrong statement about minimum labour conditions under the Ethiopian labour proclamation?
items.answer:
B. Reduction of normal hours of work will entails reduction of wages

Under Article 62(2) of the Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, reductions of normal hours of work shall not entail a reduction in the wages of a worker. This contradicts the statement that reduction of normal hours of work will entail reduction of wages.

The other statements are consistent with the law:
*   Normal working hours shall not exceed 8 hours a day or 48 hours a week (Article 61(2) of Proclamation No. 1156/2019).
*   The knowledge base does not contain a specific provision on the maximum hours for overtime work.
*   The knowledge base does not contain a specific provision on the aim to avoid premature deterioration of employees and to give room for workers to attend their social life affairs.

items.stem: Which one of the following remedies is not available for the workers who are unlawfully dismissed from their works?
items.answer:
D. Joblessness compensation

Under Article 43 of Proclamation No. 1156/2019, remedies available for unlawful termination include reinstatement and compensation. This compensation can be in addition to severance pay, as stated in Article 43(4) of Proclamation No. 1156/2019. The knowledge base does not contain a specific provision on "joblessness compensation."

items.stem: Which of the following categories of employees not governed by the labour proc. No. 1156/2019?
items.answer:
A. All.

Under Article 3(2) of the Labour Proclamation No. 1156/2019, the Proclamation is not applicable to several employment relations, including:
*   Managerial employees (Article 3(2)(c) of Proclamation No. 1156/2019).
*   Contracts of personal service (Article 3(2)(d) of Proclamation No. 1156/2019).
*   Contracts relating to persons such as members of the Armed Force, members of the Police Force, employees of state administration, judges of courts of law, prosecutors and others whose employment relationship is governed by special laws (Article 3(2)(e) of Proclamation No. 1156/2019).
*   Contracts relating to a person who performs an act, for consideration, at his own business or professional responsibility (Article 3(2)(f) of Proclamation No. 1156/2019). This category includes independent contractors.

የዚህ አንቀጽ ንዑስ አንቀጽ (1) እና (2) ድንጋጌዎች በዚህ አዋጅ አንቀጽ 137 (2) ለተመለከቱት ድርጅቶች ሠራተኞችና አሠሪዎች ተፈፃሚ አይሆኑም፡፡

citations.content:
የሚከተሉት የሥራ ውልን ያለ ማስጠንቀቂያ ለማቋረጥ በቂ ምክንያቶች ይሆናሉ:- 
ሀ) አሠሪው ወይም የሥራ መሪው የሠራተኛውን ሰብአዊ ክብርና ሞራል የሚነካ ወይም በወንጀል ሕጉ መሠረት የሚያስቀጣ ሌላ አድራጎት የፈጸመበት እንደሆነ፤ 
ለ) ሠራተኛው በአሠሪው ወይም በሥራ መሪው ወሲባዊ ትንኮሳ ወይም ጥቃት የተፈጸመበት እንደሆነ፤ 
ሐ) ለሠራተኛው ደኅንነት ወይም ጤንነት የሚያሰጋና ሊደርስ የተቃረበ አደጋ መኖሩን አሠሪው እያወቀ ወይም አደጋውን ለመከላከል የሚያስፈልጉ እርምጃዎች

citations.title: ሥራና ሠራተኛን ስለማገናኘት
citations.content:
ሥራና ሠራተኛን ማገናኘት የሚከተሉትን ይጨምራል:- 
ሥራ ፈላጊዎችንና ከአሠሪዎች የሚገለጹ ክፍት የሥራ ቦታዎችን የመመዝገብ፤
በአሠሪዎች በተገለጹ ክፍት የሥራ ቦታዎች መሠረት ከተመዘገቡትና ከቀረቡት ሥራ ፈላጊዎች መካከል መርጦ የሚመጥኑትን ለውድድር የመላክ፤ 
ማንኛውም ዕድሜው 15 እና ከዚያ በላይ የሆነ ሥራ ፈላጊ አስፈላጊውን መረጃ ሲያቀርብ አግባብ ባለው አካል የመመዝገብ፡፡
